arxiv-2007-14653.title: Relations Between Abs-Normal NLPs and MPCCs Part 2: Weak Constraint Qualifications
arxiv-2007-14653.creator: \name L.C. Hegerhorst-Schultchen a ∗ and C. Kirches b and M.C. Steinbach a
arxiv-2007-14653.description: Abstract This work continues an ongoing effort to compare non-smooth optimization problems in abs-normal form to Mathematical Programs with Complementarity Constraints (MPCCs). We study general Nonlinear Programs with equality and inequality constraints in abs-normal form, so-called Abs-Normal NLPs, and their relation to equivalent MPCC reformulations.

arxiv-2101-04798.title: Convergence analysis of some tent-based schemes for linear hyperbolic systems Thanks: This work was supported in part by NSF grant DMS-1912779.
arxiv-2101-04798.creator: Dow Drake, Jay Gopalakrishnan, Joachim Schöberl, Christoph Wintersteiger
arxiv-2101-04798.description: Abstract . Finite element methods for symmetric linear hyperbolic systems using unstructured advancing fronts (satisfying a causality condition) are considered in this work. Convergence results and error bounds are obtained for mapped tent pitching schemes made with standard discontinuous Galerkin discretizations for spatial approximation on mapped tents.

arxiv-2104-05136.title: Large evanescently-induced Brillouin scattering at the surrounding of a nanofibre
arxiv-2104-05136.creator: Fan Yang, Flavien Gyger, Adrien Godet, Jacques Chrétien, Li Zhang, Meng Pang, Jean-Charles Beugnot, Luc Thévenaz
arxiv-2104-05136.description: Abstract Brillouin scattering has been widely exploited for advanced photonics functionalities such as microwave photonics, signal processing, sensing, lasing, and more recently in micro- and nano-photonic waveguides. So far, all the works have focused on the opto-acoustic interaction driven from the core region of micro- and nano-waveguides.

arxiv-2107-05845.title: A test of Radial Acceleration Relation for the Giles et al Chandra cluster sample
arxiv-2107-05845.creator: S. Pradyumna, Shantanu Desai
arxiv-2107-05845.description: Abstract We carry out a test of the radial acceleration relation (RAR) for a sample of 10 dynamically relaxed and cool-core galaxy clusters imaged by the Chandra X-ray telescope, which was studied in Giles et al. 2017 . For this sample, we observe that the best-fit RAR shows a very tight residual scatter equal to 0.09 dex.

arxiv-2108-00535.title: A proof of Blackwell’s renewal theorem by mapping to integers
arxiv-2108-00535.creator: Rohit Pandey
arxiv-2108-00535.description: Abstract This paper presents a new proof of the renewal theorem by bijecting a general point process to a deterministic one (where the time between events is always fixed). It also provides insight into the workings of the renewal theorem.

arxiv-2204-00235.title: Production and anisotropic flow of thermal photons in collision of α \alpha -clustered carbon with heavy nuclei at relativistic energies
arxiv-2204-00235.creator: Pingal Dasgupta, Rupa Chatterjee, Guo-Liang Ma
arxiv-2204-00235.description: Abstract The presence of α \alpha -clustered structure in the light nuclei produces different exotic shapes in nuclear structure studies at low energies. Recent phenomenological studies suggest that collision of heavy nuclei with α \alpha -clustered carbon ( 12 C) at relativistic energies can lead to large initial state anisotropies.

arxiv-2302-09231.title: An explicit infinite homotopy in nonabelian Hodge theory in positive characteristic Thanks: The work is supported by National Key Research and Development Project SQ2020YFA070080, CAS Project for Young Scientists in Basic Research Grant No. YSBR-032, National Natural Science Foundation of China (Gra
arxiv-2302-09231.creator: Mao Sheng, Zebao Zhang
arxiv-2302-09231.description: Abstract . This short note is extracted from [ SZ , §3, Appendix] , where an explicit infinite homotopy from a Higgs complex to the Frobenius pushforward of the corresponding de Rham complex in positive characteristic has been provided. The verification details, which are omitted therein, are provided here.

arxiv-2402-08059.title: Learned infinite elements for helioseismology
arxiv-2402-08059.creator: D. Fournier, T. Hohage, J. Preuss, L. Gizon
arxiv-2402-08059.description: Abstract Context. Acoustic waves in the Sun are affected by the atmospheric layers, but this region is often ignored in forward models due to the increase in computational cost. Aims. The purpose of this work is to take into account the solar atmosphere without increasing significantly the computational cost. Methods.

arxiv-2406-17297.title: Towards Camera Open-set 3D Object Detection for Autonomous Driving Scenarios
arxiv-2406-17297.creator: Zhuolin He, Xinrun Li, Jiacheng Tang, Shoumeng Qiu, Wenfu Wang, Xiangyang Xue, Jian Pu *
arxiv-2406-17297.description: Abstract Conventional camera-based 3D object detectors in autonomous driving are limited to recognizing a predefined set of objects, which poses a safety risk when encountering novel or unseen objects in real-world scenarios. To address this limitation, we present OS-Det3D, a two-stage training framework designed for camera-based open-set 3D object detection.

arxiv-2410-22128.title: PF3plat: Pose-Free Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting for Novel View Synthesis
arxiv-2410-22128.creator: Sunghwan Hong, Jaewoo Jung, Heeseong Shin, Jisang Han, Jiaolong Yang †, Chong Luo †, Seungryong Kim †
arxiv-2410-22128.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sunghwan Hong, Jaewoo Jung, Heeseong Shin, Jisang Han, Jiaolong Yang †, Chong Luo †, Seungryong Kim †. We tackle the problem of view synthesis from sparse, unposed images in a single feed-forward pass. Our method builds on 3DGS and relaxes common requirements such as dense views, accurate camera poses or depth, and large image overlaps. However, the main challenge arises from the parametrization of pixel-aligned 3D Gaussians, as their misalignments inevitably yield noisy or sparse gradients that destabilize training.

arxiv-2506-01732.title: Common Corpus: The Largest Collection of Ethical Data for LLM Pre-Training
arxiv-2506-01732.creator: Pierre-Carl Langlais, Carlos Rosas Hinostroza, Mattia Nee, Catherine Arnett, Pavel Chizhov, Eliot Krzystof Jones, Irène Girard, David Mach, Anastasia Stasenko, Ivan P. Yamshchikov, PleIAs, Paris, France https://pleias.fr/
arxiv-2506-01732.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are pre-trained on large amounts of data from different sources and domains. These data most often contain trillions of tokens with large portions of copyrighted or proprietary content, which hinders the usage of such models under AI legislation. This raises the need for truly open pre-training data that is compliant with the data security regulations.

arxiv-2511-07521.title: Macdonald Index From Refined Kontsevich-Soibelman Operator
arxiv-2511-07521.creator: George Andrews, Anindya Banerjee, Ranveer Kumar Singh, Runkai Tao
arxiv-2511-07521.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by George Andrews, Anindya Banerjee, Ranveer Kumar Singh, Runkai Tao. We propose a refinement of the Kontsevich-Soibelman operator for a class of “special” 4d 𝒩 = 2 \mathcal{N}=2 superconformal field theories characterized by the following conditions: (1) their Coulomb branch admits a source/sink chamber, i.e., a chamber in which the BPS quiver consists of only source and sink nodes, (2) The nodes with valency greater than 2 of the BPS quiver in a source/sink chamber are either all sources or all sinks.

arxiv-2601-14059.title: Verifying Floating-Point Programs in Stainless
arxiv-2601-14059.creator: Andrea Gilot✉, Axel Bergström *, Eva Darulova
arxiv-2601-14059.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Andrea Gilot✉, Axel Bergström *, Eva Darulova. We extend the Stainless deductive verifier with floating-point support, providing the first automated verification support for floating-point numbers for a subset of Scala that includes polymorphism, recursion and higher-order functions. We follow the recent approach in the KeY verifier to axiomatise reasoning about mathematical functions, but go further by supporting all functions from Scala’s math API, and by verifying the correctness of the axioms against the actual implementation in Stainless itself.

arxiv-2602-06745.title: On Cartan’s Examples of Isoparametric Hypersurfaces and Their Focal Submanifolds
arxiv-2602-06745.creator: Thomas E. Cecil, Patrick J. Ryan
arxiv-2602-06745.description: Abstract This paper is a survey of Cartan’s examples of isoparametric hypersurfaces in spheres and their focal submanifolds that were described in his fundamental work on the subject, which appeared in four papers [ 2 ] – [ 5 ] published during the period 1938–1940.

pmc-10651545.creator: Konstantinos Malandris, Stylianos Papandreou, Ioannis Avgerinos, Thomas Karagiannis, Paschalis Paschos, Theodoros Michailidis, Aris Liakos, Eleni Bekiari, Emmanouil Sinakos, Apostolos Tsapas
pmc-10651545.description: PurposeTo assess the comparative efficacy of glucose-lowering drugs on liver steatosis as assessed by means of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in patients with T2D.MethodsWe searched several databases and grey literature sources. Eligible trials had at least 12 weeks of intervention, included patients with T2D, and assessed the efficacy of glucose-lowering drugs as monotherapies.

pmc-11545276.title: Enhancer of Zeste Homolog 2 Protects Mucosal Melanoma from Ferroptosis via the KLF14-SLC7A11 Signaling Pathway
pmc-11545276.creator: Haizhen Du, Lijie Hou, Huan Yu, Fenghao Zhang, Ke Tong, Xiaowen Wu, Ziyi Zhang, Kaiping Liu, Xiangguang Miao, Wenhui Guo, Jun Guo, Yan Kong, Brian Gabrielli
pmc-11545276.description: Simple SummaryMucosal melanoma is a rare and aggressive form of melanoma that is different from the more common skin melanoma. Unfortunately, current treatments have not significantly improved outcomes for patients with this disease. Our research focuses on understanding the biological mechanisms that drive mucosal melanoma and finding new treatment strategies.

pmc-11555138.title: Improved diagnostic performance of high‐sensitivity cardiac troponins in muscle dystrophies using comprehensive definition criteria for cardiac involvement: A longitudinal study on 35 patients
pmc-11555138.creator: Mustafa Yildirim, Christian Salbach, Christoph Reich, Regina Pribe‐Wolferts, Barbara Ruth Milles, Tobias Täger, Matthias Mueller‐Hennessen, Markus Weiler, Benjamin Meder, Norbert Frey, Evangelos Giannitsis
pmc-11555138.description: Background and purposeSparse information is available on the correct interpretation of elevated high‐sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs‐cTn) in confirmed muscular dystrophies.MethodsSerum concentrations of hs‐cTn T (hs‐cTnT) and hs‐cTn I (hs‐cTnI) were determined in 35 stable outpatients with confirmed skeletal muscle dystrophies.

pmc-12484169.title: Neutrophil-to-albumin ratio: a novel predictor of osteoporosis in rheumatoid arthritis
pmc-12484169.creator: Yifang Zhang, Zhongyu He, Kaiqiang Li, Qiuping Wu, Shigang Wang, Minying Liu, Qingping Liu, Qiang Xu, Xiangying Kong, Changsong Lin
pmc-12484169.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundOsteoporosis (OP) frequently coexists with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but validated predictors of early risk are not extensively studied. This study seeks to examine the relationship between the neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio (NPAR) and the likelihood of developing RA-related OP(RA-OP).MethodsAfter investigating the relationship between the NPAR and RA-OP in the clinical retrospective study, we further validated this association using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) database (2005-2020 cycles).

pmc-12808363.title: Students’ stress prediction and explainable analysis based on improved decision trees
pmc-12808363.creator: Cheng Liu, Shuang Yu
pmc-12808363.description: IntroductionNowadays students are burdened with pressures from various aspects such as academics, social life, and career planning. It is of great significance to accurately predict their stress levels and analyze the key influencing factors.MethodsA stress prediction model for students was constructed based on an enhanced decision tree (DT) algorithm.

pmc-13550500.creator: L Elesin, A L Shilov, M Kravtsov, X Zhou, M Lukianov, A Kuksov, S Jana, I Iorsh, R Izmaylov, K Shein, I Gayduchenko, T Taniguchi, K Watanabe, K S Novoselov, G N Goltsman, A Principi, D A Bandurin
